beats.note: walk with them and let it come up
beats.text: {N} has been getting letters. You have not seen anybody deliver one. 'Old employer,' they say, folding it away. 'There is paperwork. There is always paperwork.'

beats.note: keep them in fights and see what slips
beats.text: {N} stops mid-swing and apologises to nobody in particular. Afterwards, unprompted: 'Not to you. There is a clause about enthusiasm and I am told I have been exceeding it.'

beats.note: take them to {P}
beats.text: {N} regards {P} the way most people regard a dentist. 'This is where I signed. I would like the original back, and I would like to not discuss why on the walk in.'

endings.label: Burn it in front of them
endings.text: The document goes up fast, the way old paper does. {N} watches every word of it catch, then works their jaw like somebody testing a new tooth. The letters stop. Something quieter starts, and they do not mention it.

endings.label: Sell it back to the estate
endings.text: The estate pays promptly, which tells you what the contract was worth. {N} takes the news like a professional, which is to say entirely, and calls you 'employer' for a week afterwards without once making it sound like a compliment.

beats.note: walk with them and let it come up
beats.text: {N} will not eat in front of anyone. On the fourth night they explain that it is not a religious thing, it is a scheduling thing, and then they explain nothing further for two days.

beats.note: put down {X} where they can count them
beats.text: {N} counts each {X} out loud as it goes down. At three they stop counting and look relieved in a way that does not suit their face at all.

beats.note: take them to {P}
beats.text: '{P},' says {N}. 'Witnessed here. Do not sign anything, do not accept a drink, and whatever else happens, do not compliment the furniture.'

endings.label: Buy out the terms
endings.text: The sum is large and the receipt is a small cold weight in your pocket for about an hour before it stops existing. {N} does not thank you. They do start eating in front of people, which from them is a speech.

endings.label: Let it stand
endings.text: The arrangement continues, and the arrangement pays. {N} accepts this the way you accept weather. 'It was always going to,' they say. 'That is the shape of it.' They are cheerful for a week, which is much worse.

beats.note: walk with them and let it come up
beats.text: {N} has started sleeping outside the camp, facing out. They say the fire ruins their night vision. This is true. It is not the reason.

beats.note: walk them into a town and watch
beats.text: In the street somebody calls {N} by a name you did not hire. {N} does not turn round, does not break stride, and does not say another word for four streets.

beats.note: take them to {P}
beats.text: {P}. {N} goes quiet a hundred paces out and stays quiet. Then: 'They will be smaller than I remember. Everything is. I would like to get this over with.'

endings.label: Go in with them
endings.text: It is dark and it smells of animal and old smoke, and whatever meeting happens in there happens in a language with no words in it. {N} comes out walking differently. They do not explain and you do not ask.

endings.label: Wait outside
endings.text: You wait. It takes a while. {N} comes out alone carrying something wrapped, sells it in the next town without discussion, and hands you the larger half. Neither of you raises the subject again.

threads.title: The Favour They Cannot Ask For

beats.note: walk with them and let it come up
beats.text: {N} cannot lie, as they mention often, in sentences built with the care of a load-bearing wall. Tonight one of them fails halfway through and they sit down in the road.

beats.note: keep them in fights and see what slips
beats.text: 'I am glad you are alive,' says {N} after the fight, and then stands very still, apparently checking whether it went through unchallenged.

beats.note: take them to {P}
beats.text: At {P} something is owed to {N} that they are not permitted to ask for, on account of asking being a kind of lying if you already know the answer. They look at you meaningfully. That is the whole of it.

endings.label: Ask on their behalf
endings.text: You ask. It is a small thing, said out loud, and the thing at {P} hands it over with the bad grace of a clerk at closing. {N} does not thank you, because that would also be a kind of lying, and instead is unbearably pleasant for a month.

endings.label: Make them find the words
endings.text: It takes {N} most of an hour and it is not comfortable to watch. What they eventually construct is technically true, structurally magnificent, and answered with something heavy and unpleasantly warm. They insist you take half.

beats.note: walk with them and let it come up
beats.text: {N} keeps a jar. The jar, in a sense they decline to unpack, also keeps {N}. It is corked. It is always the last thing packed and the first thing checked.

beats.note: put down {X} where they can see
beats.text: {N} holds the jar up to each {X} as it falls, the way you show a child a parade. 'He would have liked that one,' they say, of nobody you have met.

beats.note: take them to {P}
beats.text: '{P},' says {N}, and sets the jar down on a rock with enormous care. 'He asked to be brought here. He asked a lot of things. This is the one I can still do.'

endings.label: Help them bury it
endings.text: The ground is bad and it takes both of you the better part of the afternoon. {N} says a few words that are mostly logistics. Afterwards they are lighter by about a jar, and by rather more than that.

endings.label: Tell them to keep it
endings.text: {N} thinks about it for a long moment and then packs the jar away again, visibly relieved and visibly ashamed of being relieved. Somebody in the next town pays absurdly well for a look at it. You split that.

beats.note: walk with them and let it come up
beats.text: {N} has been counting their own steps since the day you hired them and will tell you the number if asked. It is correct. It has been correct every time you have checked.

beats.note: walk them into a town and watch
beats.text: A man in a good coat follows you for two streets, writing, and leaves when {N} looks at him. 'They keep notes,' {N} says. 'I would quite like to read them. I am the subject.'

beats.note: take them to {P}
beats.text: The notes are at {P}, in a box, in an order somebody thought about. {N} stands in front of it with their hands behind their back like a person at a graveside.

endings.label: Burn the notes unread
endings.text: {N} does not read a page of it, which you suspect took more out of them than the walk. The fire is brief and thorough. 'Now nobody has established what,' they say, apparently pleased. 'Including me.'

endings.label: Sell them to the college
endings.text: The college pays without haggling, which is how you learn what {N} is worth on paper. {N} reads the receipt with great interest and asks to keep it. They are noticeably easier company and noticeably more expensive.

beats.note: walk with them and let it come up
beats.text: {N} counts their cut twice every time, and puts most of it somewhere that is not a pocket. Asked about it, they say 'it is spoken for' in the voice of somebody quoting.

beats.note: keep them in fights and see what slips
beats.text: {N} takes a bad hit and says a name on the way down. It is not yours and it is not theirs, and when they get up they are extremely keen to talk about anything else.

beats.note: take them to {P}
beats.text: The sum is owed in {P}, and has been for long enough to have grown a personality. {N} is very calm about this in the way of somebody who has rehearsed being calm about it.

endings.label: Settle it out of the purse
endings.text: The debt is smaller than the dread of it, which is how debts work. {N} watches it get paid, says 'right', and then says 'right' again about ten minutes later, out on the road, to nobody.

endings.label: Introduce yourself to the creditor
endings.text: You have a conversation. It is not a long one and nothing is broken. The terms afterwards are extremely reasonable, and {N} looks at you for the rest of the day as though recalculating something.

beats.note: walk with them and let it come up
beats.text: {N} asks, casually, whether {X} ever drops {I}. Then asks again the next day, and the day after that, each time as though for the first.

beats.note: put down {X} until they say when
beats.text: Three of them down, and {N} has been through all three with a knife and an expression of mounting professional disappointment. 'Not that one either.'

beats.note: take them to {P}
beats.text: 'The big one is at {P},' says {N}. 'It has been at {P} for eleven years. I have been not going to {P} for eleven years. Those two facts are related.'

endings.label: Let them take the shot
endings.text: {N} takes it. It is not clean and it is not quick and nobody says anything encouraging while it is happening. Afterwards they hold up {I} in both hands and look at it for a very long time, and then put it in a pocket like a receipt.

endings.label: Take it yourself and hand it over
endings.text: You do it. It is easier than it should be, and that is the problem: {N} is grateful, thoroughly and out loud, and something goes out of them that you cannot put back. They ask for a bigger share the following week and you give it.

beats.note: walk them into a town and watch
beats.text: {N} does not go into the tavern. {N} waits outside the tavern, at an angle, with a view of both doors, and is unable to give a reason that survives being said out loud.

beats.note: walk with them and let it come up
beats.text: The name you hired {N} under is on a list somewhere, they explain, along with a description that is unfair and a sum that is not. The sum is the part they resent.

beats.note: take them to {P}
beats.text: The list is kept in {P}, and so is the man who keeps it. {N} points this out, waits, and then adds: 'I am not asking. I am describing a situation.'

endings.label: Have the name struck off
endings.text: It costs what it costs and the clerk does not look up once. {N} reads the amended page twice, mouths their own name off it, and is unreasonably good company for a fortnight.

endings.label: Have it sold to somebody else
endings.text: There is always a market for a name with a sum attached. The buyer is delighted, the clerk is incurious, and {N} is now legally somebody with a much worse reputation and considerably more money.

beats.note: come back when you have seen a few
beats.text: {N} does not introduce themselves. '{X},' they say. 'You have seen one. I can tell, you have the look.' They tap the floorboards twice with a heel. 'There is one under here. Has been for eleven years. It pays rent.'

beats.note: put down four of {X}, then go back to {N}
beats.text: 'Four,' says {N}, counting on fingers that have done this before. 'Four is enough to know. They do not scream, do they. They just stop.' A long pause. 'Mine screams. So either mine is different, or the rest of them are being polite.'

endings.label: Go down and look
endings.text: The cellar is dry and cold and entirely empty except for a chair, which is warm. {N} takes this news standing up, then sits down on the floor of their own kitchen and stays there a while. 'Eleven years,' they say. 'I could have just gone down.'

endings.label: Tell them it is nothing
endings.text: 'Nothing,' repeats {N}, and you can watch them decide to believe it. They pay you for the trouble out of a tin kept for exactly this, which suggests you are not the first. The floorboards do not come up.

beats.note: go to {P}, then come back and tell {N}
beats.text: 'You will be going out that way,' says {N}. It is not a question. 'My brother went to {P}. Eight months ago. He was not a brave man, which is why I have not gone to look — I am the one he got it from.'

beats.note: go to {P}, then come back and tell {N}
beats.text: There is a name scratched into the wall by the entrance, and under it, in the same hand and a great deal deeper, a second attempt at the same name. Nothing else in the place has been touched in years.

endings.label: Tell them exactly what you found
endings.text: {N} listens to all of it, including the part about the second scratch, and does not cry until you have finished, which you suspect was deliberate. Then they feed you, at length, and refuse every coin you offer, also at length.

endings.label: Tell them he made it further than that
endings.text: It costs you nothing to say and {N} takes hold of it with both hands. They tell the neighbours. The neighbours tell people. Somewhere out there is a version of that brother who died gloriously, and it is doing very well for itself.

beats.note: come back through here when you have been out a while
beats.text: 'You are the fourth person through this month,' says {N}, 'so I will say it to you as well.' They put a wrapped parcel on the counter. 'Paid for in advance, eleven years ago, by somebody who said they would be back on the Thursday. Which Thursday was not specified.'

beats.note: go and be somewhere else for a while, then come back
beats.text: The parcel is on the counter again, in exactly the same place, and {N} has clearly been putting it away and getting it out. '{I},' they say, before you ask. 'That is what is in it. I looked, in year six. I have felt terrible ever since and I would do it again.'

endings.label: Buy it off them
endings.text: {N} takes the money like somebody being talked down off a ledge, and puts the parcel into your hands with both of theirs. 'If he comes back,' they say, 'I will send him to you.' The counter looks enormous now, and empty.

endings.label: Tell them to keep waiting
endings.text: 'Right,' says {N}. 'Right.' The parcel goes back under the counter. They are visibly relieved, which is the worst part of the whole exchange, and they insist on paying you for the conversation.

beats.note: let them get another look at you
beats.text: {N} watches you the whole way across the room and carries on after you have stopped being interesting. 'You are not from here either,' they say eventually. 'Do not worry. Nobody has worked out that I am not, and I have had nineteen years to give myself away.'

beats.note: come back through this town again
beats.text: 'Nineteen years,' says {N}, picking it up as though no time has passed, which for them it has not. 'I have a whole family here. They think I am from the coast. I am not from the coast. I have never seen the coast.' They look at you levelly. 'You have been out. Is it there?'

endings.label: Tell them what is out there
endings.text: You describe it. {N} takes it in the way somebody takes a diagnosis — carefully, and without interrupting once. At the end they say 'good' twice, meaning it differently each time, and go back to work with the look of a person who has stopped waiting for something.

endings.label: Ask what they are hiding from
endings.text: {N} tells you. It takes a while, none of it is your business, and by the end you are holding a good deal more of it than you meant to. There is money involved, historically, and some of it is still in a box under a floor in this town.
